claim: Let \(h,k\ge 2\) with \(h\ne k\). Let \(P=A_1\oplus\cdots\oplus A_h\) and \(Q=B_1\oplus\cdots\oplus B_k\) be finite weak orders, where every level \(A_i\) and \(B_j\) is an antichain of cardinality at least two and every point of a lower level is below every point of a higher level. Then every continuous map \(f:P\to Q\) is homotopic, as a map of finite spaces, to a constant map. More strongly, for every \(f\) there is a fence in the pointwise-ordered finite mapping space \(Q^P\) from \(f\) to a constant map using at most three comparability edges. Consequently \(Q^P\) is path connected and the unbased finite-space homotopy set \([P,Q]\) is a singleton.

integrity.novelty_boundary: The previously known binary-source special case is not claimed as new; the extension to arbitrary source-level cardinalities and the uniform three-edge fence bound are the new content assessed here.
integrity.proof_core: A singleton occupied target level gives a two-edge contraction. A source level spanning target levels can be perturbed upward to create such a singleton. Otherwise source levels inject strictly into target levels; unequal heights then force either impossibility or an omitted target level that creates a singleton after one comparison.
integrity.verification_scope: Exhaustive constructive-fence replay on 11,435 order-preserving maps across seven unequal-height weak-order pairs.

scientific_limitations: Equal-height weak orders are excluded and can have non-null isolated map classes.
Every source and target level is assumed to have cardinality at least two.
The theorem concerns direct finite-space homotopy and not maps after subdivision or weak replacement.
Finite enumeration is a stress test only; the general statement rests on the symbolic fence construction.
title: Cross-height nullity for finite weak-order pseudospheres
